options: dbt's mechanism for capturing row-level history over time — its own version of the SCD Type 2 pattern
A backup of the entire warehouse taken nightly
A test that checks a model's row count hasn't changed
A screenshot of the dbt Cloud IDE saved for documentation
questions.explain: A snapshot is dbt's own mechanism for SCD Type 2 — instead of hand-writing the close-out-then-insert UPDATE/INSERT pair, one config generates and runs that logic for you.

questions.q: When should you use the `check` strategy instead of `timestamp`?
options: When the source has no trustworthy updated_at column, so dbt compares actual column values instead
When you want dbt to skip change detection entirely
Only when the source table has fewer than 100 rows
check and timestamp always produce identical results, so it never matters
questions.explain: The check strategy compares the actual values of the columns you list, which is exactly what you need when there's no reliable updated_at column to trust.

questions.q: What does a null `dbt_valid_to` mean on a snapshot row?
options: That row is the current version — it hasn't been superseded yet
The row failed to load correctly
The row was deleted from the source
dbt could not determine a strategy for that row
questions.explain: dbt_valid_to records when a version was superseded; null means it hasn't been superseded, so it's the current version.

questions.q: Why does check_cols: all tend to be a worse choice than listing specific columns?
options: It's more expensive and can trigger new versions from irrelevant column changes
check_cols: all is not valid dbt syntax
It disables the timestamp strategy permanently
It only works with seeds, not snapshots
questions.explain: Comparing every column costs more and records a new version whenever any column changes, including ones that don't actually matter for tracking history.

questions.q: Why must a snapshot be run on a recurring schedule to be useful?
options: Because it only captures a change if the source row differs the next time it runs — a snapshot run once is just a one-time copy, not a history
Because dbt snapshot deletes its own results after 24 hours
Because snapshots require a live network connection to function at all
Scheduling is optional and has no effect on what history is captured
questions.explain: A snapshot only sees a change between runs — it can't retroactively reconstruct history, so it has to run regularly (via a scheduled job) to actually build up a history.
